articles.title: Fauci takes Fifth Amendment, refuses to answer Senate panel questions
articles.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci, who led the nation's infectious disease efforts during the pandemic, invoked the Fifth Amendment on Wednesday and declined to answer questions from a Senate committee investigating the origins of COVID-19. Why it matters: Fauci said Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.), the head of the Senate homeland security committee, was trying to get him to say something that could put him in legal jeopardy. Former President Biden gave Fauci a preemptive pardon before leaving office, but Fauci argues he could be in trouble if he makes any statements that could open new lines of investigation for the committee. What he's saying: Paul has an "unhinged obsession with me," and his motive for the hearing is to "get me to say something — anything — that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, quote, behind bars unquote," Fauci said. "Although it pains me to do so ... under the advice of my attorneys, I will invoke my right under the Fifth Amendment of the Constitution to refrain from answering your questions," Fauci said. The other side: "There will be repercussions to your refusal to testify today," Paul told Fauci. This is breaking news. Check back for updates.

articles.title: Situation in Middle East comes under discussion as DPM Dar meets Kuwait FM
articles.description: The situation in the Middle East came under discussion as Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday met Kuwait’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah, who is on an official visit to the country. According to the Foreign Office (FO), the two held a “warm and productive” tête-à-tête at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. “The two leaders reviewed the full spectrum of Pakistan–Kuwait bilateral relations and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening the longstanding brotherly partnership,” it said. “They also held in-depth discussions on regional and international developments, with particular focus on the evolving situation in the Middle East,” it added. The visiting dignitary arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday at the invitation of Deputy PM Dar. The FO said that upon arrival at the Islamabad International Airport, he was received by Zahid Hussain, additional secretary at the foreign ministry. It added that the minister’s visit to Pakistan reflected the longstanding brotherly relations between the two countries, “anchored in shared history, mutual trust and close cooperation”. Announcing the visit on Monday, the FO said Kuwait’s top diplomat was expected to pay a courtesy call on the leadership of Pakistan. Pakistan has been negotiating an expanded defence pact with Kuwait in exchange for energy cooperation and investment, the Reuters news agency reported earlier this month, citing five sources with knowledge of the talks.

articles.title: Suddenly the British right feels a political chill. It’s getting cold in Andy Burnham’s shadow | Rafael Behr
articles.description: The Tories and Reform had it easy when Keir Starmer was self-destructing – but a new PM with ideas exposes how vacant the opposition has become Andy Burnham’s recollections of Britain in the 1970s must be pretty hazy. He was nine when the decade ended. Kemi Badenoch, born in 1980, can remember nothing. Lacking first-hand experience, the Conservative leader evokes the turmoil of a bygone era with cautionary zeal borrowed from an older generation. In a speech last week, she accused the new prime minister of pining for “endless strikes, rubbish not being collected, bodies not being buried, inflation at 25% and a chancellor going cap-in-hand to the IMF”. This is more incantation than argument, a ritual fondling of beads on the Tory rosary. It is a symptom of a leader under stress, affirming her faith in Our Lady Margaret Thatcher and warding off socialist devils. Burnham has done nothing to support the claim that his government is a 70s tribute act, unless you count the appointment of a man named Healey as chancellor and the imposition of price controls on buses. Rafael Behr is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

articles.title: 'Get it done!' Trump fumes at Senate Republicans blocking 'first step' for election plot
articles.description: President Donald Trump fumed at Senate Republicans on Tuesday over their continued blockage of his legislative agenda. Trump has repeatedly called for Senate Republicans to pass his SAVE Act, which would overhaul the way U.S. elections are conducted, before their August recess. However, Republicans have shot down those calls , arguing that there are not 60 votes to pass the bill and that they are unwilling to eliminate the filibuster to do so. Trump claimed in a post on Truth Social that Sen. Ron Johnson (R-WI) has a scheme up his sleeve to pass part of the bill before the recess, which he called a "critical first step." He then fumed at Republicans to "get it done!" "Senator Ron Johnson is working hard with Senate Republican Leadership to adopt a Budget Resolution before the August recess," Trump wrote. "This is the first step towards getting as much of THE SAVE AMERICA ACT as possible in a Budget Bill, funding our Troops, and helping our Farmers." "I am calling on the Senate to get this critical first step done before the August recess," he added. "This Resolution can be adopted at a simple Majority threshold. GET IT DONE!"

articles.title: Dire warning as Trump's latest Supreme Court-blessed project creates 'modern pogrom'
articles.description: President Donald Trump is planning a brutal crackdown on a class of immigrants who have never broken any laws, warned an expert. This term, the Supreme Court ruled the president can summarily choose to end temporary protected status for Haitians, plowing over congressional language making clear that TPS only ends when conditions in the home country become materially safe, which even Trump's own State Department does not believe . As of today, the Trump administration has officially canceled that status, and while many migrants who previously qualified for TPS could theoretically apply for other forms of residency, American Immigration Council senior fellow Aaron Reichlin-Melnick said on X the intent is clear: it's open season on deporting them. He pointed to reporting from the Washington Examiner that Immigration and Customs Enforcement activity is immediately surging to communities with large Haitian populations, like portions of Queens and Brooklyn. "ICE's decision to 'blitz' communities where Haitians have been living and working legally for years is a modern pogrom targeting a disfavored ethnic group," said Reichlin-Melnick. "They won't be targeting criminals, or 'bad guys.' It'll be nurses, students, people who passed multiple backgrounds [sic] checks." Trump has expressed open racism toward Haiti for years. He reportedly described the country with an expletive , and spread a viral hoax about Haitian workers in Springfield, Ohio, eating people's dogs and cats .
